```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.align = "center"
)

library(ggplot2)

# Prepare data once: treat cylinders as a categorical variable
mt <- mtcars
mt$cyl <- factor(mt$cyl)

# Reusable theme and mean value
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
mean_mpg <- mean(mt$mpg)
```

# Introduction

## Objective
Demonstrate nine `ggplot2` geoms and show what each reveals about fuel efficiency (`mpg`) in the built-in `mtcars` dataset.

## Data
`mtcars` contains `r nrow(mt)` cars and `r ncol(mt)` variables, taken from the 1974 *Motor Trend* magazine.

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mpg` | Continuous | Miles per US gallon |
| `cyl` | Categorical | Number of cylinders (4, 6, 8) |
| `wt` | Continuous | Weight (1000 lbs) |

```{r glimpse}
str(mt[, c("mpg", "cyl", "wt")])
```

## Plot Pattern
Every plot follows the same structure: `ggplot(data, aes(...)) + geom_*()`, with layers stacked using `+`.

# Distributions of One Variable

## Bar Chart: Cars per Cylinder Group
`geom_bar()` counts observations in each category.

```{r bar}
ggplot(mt, aes(cyl)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Number of Cars by Cylinder Count",
       x = "Cylinders", y = "Count")
```

**Interpretation:** 8-cylinder cars are the most common in this sample and 6-cylinder cars the least.

## Histogram: Distribution of MPG
`geom_histogram()` bins a continuous variable and counts values per bin.

```{r histogram}
ggplot(mt, aes(mpg)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Miles per Gallon",
       x = "Miles per Gallon", y = "Count")
```

**Interpretation:** MPG is slightly right-skewed, with most cars between roughly 15 and 25 mpg and a few efficient outliers.

## Density with Rug: Smoothed Distribution
`geom_density()` smooths the histogram, and `geom_rug()` marks each individual observation along the axis.

```{r density}
ggplot(mt, aes(mpg)) +
  geom_density(fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_rug() +
  labs(title = "Density of Miles per Gallon",
       subtitle = "Rug ticks show individual cars",
       x = "Miles per Gallon", y = "Density")
```

**Interpretation:** The density shows the same shape as the histogram without depending on bin choice. The rug shows where individual cars sit.

## Histogram with Mean Line
`geom_vline()` adds a vertical reference line, here at the mean.

```{r vline}
ggplot(mt, aes(mpg)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_mpg, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of MPG with Mean Marked",
       subtitle = paste("Mean =", round(mean_mpg, 1), "mpg"),
       x = "Miles per Gallon", y = "Count")
```

**Interpretation:** The mean is about `r round(mean_mpg, 1)` mpg, and the dashed line splits the distribution near its center.

# Comparing a Continuous Variable Across Groups

## Boxplot: MPG by Cylinder
`geom_boxplot()` shows the median, quartiles, and outliers for each group.

```{r boxplot}
ggplot(mt, aes(cyl, mpg, fill = cyl)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Fuel Efficiency by Number of Cylinders",
       x = "Cylinders", y = "Miles per Gallon")
```

**Interpretation:** Median MPG falls as cylinder count rises. 4-cylinder cars are the most efficient, and 8-cylinder cars are the least.

## Violin with Jitter: Shape and Raw Points
`geom_violin()` shows the distribution shape per group, and `geom_jitter()` overlays the raw points with a small horizontal offset to reduce overlap.

```{r violin}
ggplot(mt, aes(cyl, mpg)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey90") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.7, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "MPG Distribution by Cylinder Group",
       subtitle = "Violin shows shape; points show individual cars",
       x = "Cylinders", y = "Miles per Gallon")
```

**Interpretation:** The 4-cylinder group has the widest spread. The 6-cylinder group has only a few points, so its violin shape should be read cautiously.

# Relationship Between Two Continuous Variables

## Scatterplot with Mean Reference Line
`geom_point()` plots each car, and `geom_hline()` adds a horizontal reference line at mean MPG.

```{r hline}
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean_mpg, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Weight vs Fuel Efficiency",
       subtitle = "Dashed line marks mean MPG",
       x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "Miles per Gallon")
```

**Interpretation:** Heavier cars tend to have lower MPG. The correlation is about `r round(cor(mt$wt, mt$mpg), 2)`, a strong negative relationship.

## Line Plot: MPG as Weight Increases
`geom_line()` connects points in order along the x-axis, so the data must be sorted first.

```{r line}
cars_sorted <- mt[order(mt$wt), ]

ggplot(cars_sorted, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "MPG Ordered by Vehicle Weight",
       x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "Miles per Gallon")
```

**Interpretation:** The overall trend is downward, but the line is jagged because it connects separate cars. This is not a time series, so a scatterplot with `geom_smooth()` is usually the better choice.

## Text Labels: Identifying Individual Cars
`geom_text()` prints a label at each point, here the car name.

```{r text, fig.height=6}
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg, label = rownames(mt))) +
  geom_text(size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Weight vs MPG with Car Names",
       x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "Miles per Gallon")
```

**Interpretation:** Labels make it easy to spot individual cars, such as the lightest and most efficient models. Overlap is a problem with 32 points, and `ggrepel::geom_text_repel()` would fix it.

# Summary

| Geom | Purpose | Best used for |
|---|---|---|
| `geom_bar()` | Count categories | One categorical variable |
| `geom_histogram()` | Bin and count | One continuous variable |
| `geom_density()` | Smoothed distribution | Comparing shapes |
| `geom_rug()` | Mark each observation | Adding to density or scatter |
| `geom_boxplot()` | Median, quartiles, outliers | Continuous by category |
| `geom_violin()` | Distribution shape | Continuous by category |
| `geom_jitter()` | Raw points, spread out | Overlaying on groups |
| `geom_vline()`, `geom_hline()` | Reference lines | Marking a mean or threshold |
| `geom_point()` | Individual observations | Two continuous variables |
| `geom_line()` | Connect ordered points | Time series or sorted data |
| `geom_text()` | Label points | Identifying observations |

**Key findings**

1. Fuel efficiency decreases as cylinder count and vehicle weight increase.
2. Most cars in the sample fall between roughly 15 and 25 mpg.
3. Different geoms answer different questions, so combine them (for example violin plus jitter) for a fuller picture.
